title: L7 Capstone: Mini App Suite
story: You've built calculators, games, timers, and converters. Now build a MENU that ties five of your favorite tools into one program. Pick an option, run that tool, return to menu. This is how real applications work — a launcher for your growing toolkit.
why: The app suite capstone demonstrates program composition, menu-driven architecture, and the ability to orchestrate multiple subsystems — the pattern behind every multi-feature application.
analogy: A Swiss Army knife: each tool (blade, scissors, screwdriver, corkscrew) is independently useful, but they live together in one compact body. The menu is the knife body. You pick which tool to deploy. Close it, and pick another. Your App Suite is the digital Swiss Army knife.
try_it: Add more apps from L7 (Unit Converter, Grade Calculator, Budget Tracker). Add a settings menu (difficulty, decimal places). Track usage statistics: which app is used most? Add persistent state — todo items survive between menu returns.
tips: The menu is a while loop + print + dispatch — simple, effective, extensible
Each app function should be self-contained — returns to menu when done
This pattern scales: add more options without restructuring the menu loop
common_mistakes: Apps that don't return to the menu — each must complete and yield control
Hardcoding choices in the main loop without a read_input mechanism
Not handling invalid choices — 'else' catches anything not in 1-5
